newsitem.title: GERMANY: German unions urge Bonn not to cut spending.
newsitem.headline: German unions urge Bonn not to cut spending.

text.p: Germany's Trade Union Federation (DGB) urged Bonn on Thursday not to choke off economic growth and jobs by introducing drastic savings because of an 18 billion mark ($10.6 billion) tax revenue shortfall this year.

DGB board member Michael Geuenich said in a statement that Bonn should not cut back public spending to balance out the shortfall, which threatened Germany's chances to qualify for Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
"We must not choke off growth and the labour market with savings," he said, adding the DGB already saw Germany in a downward spiral of "saving, weak growth, unemployment and saving again."
Geuenich said the DGB saw new borrowing or sales of assets as being equally effective in counteracting the shortfall.
